question: What is the term for programmed cell death regulated by the body?
explanation: Apoptosis is the controlled process the body uses to eliminate damaged or unneeded cells safely. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why are cell cycle checkpoints vital for normal tissue health?

options.A: They speed up the rate of tissue healing
options.B: They increase the size of aging cells
options.C: They supply extra blood to active tissues
options.D: They stop cells from dividing with damaged DNA

explanation: Checkpoints halt the cell cycle to allow for DNA repair or trigger cell death if damage is severe. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which feature is most characteristic of a benign tumor?
explanation: Benign tumors are typically enclosed within a fibrous capsule that keeps them localized. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h2)

question: A biopsy report shows poorly differentiated cells with irregular borders. What does this mean?

options.A: A malignant neoplasm with invasive traits
options.B: A benign growth healing from chronic inflammation

explanation: Poor differentiation and irregular borders are hallmark signs of malignancy and tissue invasion. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h2)

question: What happens when a proto-oncogene undergoes a mutation?

options.A: It triggers immediate programmed cell death
options.B: It becomes an oncogene that promotes rapid cell growth
options.C: It halts all protein synthesis in the cell
options.D: It transforms into a tumor suppressor gene

explanation: Mutations convert normal proto-oncogenes into overactive oncogenes that drive cancer development. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h3)

question: How do tumor suppressor genes normally protect the human body?

options.A: By stimulating new blood vessel growth to injured areas
options.B: By slowing cell division and repairing damaged DNA
options.C: By speeding up the transport of nutrients into cells
options.D: By producing antibodies against abnormal proteins

explanation: Tumor suppressor genes act as molecular brakes to prevent uncontrolled cellular proliferation. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h3)

question: What occurs during the initiation phase of carcinogenesis?

options.A: New blood vessels form to feed the mass
options.B: Tumor cells spread to distant lymph nodes
options.C: The immune system destroys the mutated cells
options.D: Permanent DNA damage occurs in a cell

explanation: Initiation involves irreversible genetic damage caused by exposure to a carcinogen. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why is the promotion phase of cancer development considered reversible?

options.A: Removing the promoting stimulus can slow down repeated cell division
options.B: The body clears out all altered cells through normal digestion
options.C: Initiated cells automatically repair their DNA during this time
options.D: Immune responses permanently eliminate the tumor mass

explanation: Promotion relies on continuous exposure to growth stimuli, which can sometimes be reduced or stopped. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of tumor angiogenesis?

options.A: To shrink the overall size of the malignant lesion
options.B: To supply oxygen and nutrients to the growing mass
options.C: To remove waste products away from healthy tissue
options.D: To transport immune cells directly into the tumor core

explanation: Angiogenesis creates new blood vessels necessary to sustain the metabolic needs of a growing tumor. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which chemical signal stimulates new vessel growth in tumors?
explanation: Tumor cells secrete vascular endothelial growth factor to signal nearby blood vessels to sprout branches. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h5)

question: What enzymes do cancer cells use to break through the extracellular matrix during invasion?
explanation: Matrix metalloproteinases degrade structural proteins in the extracellular matrix, clearing a path for tumor invasion. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the term for cancer cells entering local blood or lymphatic vessels?
explanation: Intravasation describes cancer cells breaching vessel walls to enter the circulatory system. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which cells are primarily responsible for destroying abnormal and cancerous cells in the body?
explanation: Cytotoxic T lymphocytes play a key role in cell-mediated immunity by targeting and destroying malignant cells. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h7)

question: How do some tumor cells avoid being destroyed by the immune system?

options.A: By speeding up the normal metabolic rate of the liver
options.B: By forming a thick outer capsule made of red blood cells
options.C: By downregulating their abnormal surface antigens
options.D: By increasing their production of normal body hormones

explanation: Reducing or altering surface antigens prevents immune cells from recognizing the cancer as foreign. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h7)
